tagging_basis: OCR H432 numbered specification sections (lettered learning outcomes as evidence)

units.label: 1(a)
units.summary: Explain in terms of electron transfer whether nickel is oxidised or reduced when it reacts with HCl.
units.difficulty_basis: Single-mark recall of oxidation as electron loss

units.label: 1(b)(i)
units.summary: Calculate the minimum volume of HCl needed to react completely with a given mass of nickel.

units.label: 1(b)(ii)
units.summary: Calculate the volume of hydrogen at RTP from moles of nickel.

units.label: 1(b)(iii)
units.summary: State and explain whether magnesium gives a different volume of hydrogen with the same acid volume.

units.label: 1(c)
units.summary: Describe tests to identify bromide, sulfate and carbonate anions and give equations.
units.difficulty_basis: Standard anion tests but six marks with equations

units.label: 2(a)
units.summary: Explain the term enthalpy change of combustion.

units.label: 2(b)
units.summary: Calculate the enthalpy change of combustion of cyclohexane from calorimetry data.
units.difficulty_basis: q = mcDT then per mole with sign and 3 sf

units.label: 2(c)(i)
units.summary: Compare the percentage uncertainty of the temperature change with that of the water volume.

units.label: 2(c)(ii)
units.summary: Suggest two reasons other than measurement uncertainty why the experimental value is less exothermic.

units.label: 2(c)(iii)
units.summary: Explain whether heating the water for longer would improve the accuracy of the result.
units.difficulty_basis: Balancing competing effects of uncertainty and heat loss

units.label: 3(a)
units.summary: Explain the melting point and conductivity of calcium and bromine using structure and bonding.
units.difficulty_basis: Compare two structure types over three points

units.label: 3(b)(i)
units.summary: Draw a dot-and-cross diagram for calcium bromide showing outer electrons.

units.label: 3(b)(ii)
units.summary: Explain why barium reacts more vigorously with bromine than calcium.
units.difficulty_basis: Comparative argument on radius shielding and ionisation energy

units.label: 3(c)(i)
units.summary: Write the equation for aluminium selenide reacting with water.
units.difficulty_basis: Balanced equation for an unfamiliar reaction

units.label: 3(c)(ii)
units.summary: Explain why water has a higher boiling point than hydrogen selenide.
units.difficulty_basis: Comparison of hydrogen bonding and London forces

units.label: 3(d)(i)
units.summary: Write the systematic name for NaBrO3.

units.label: 3(d)(ii)
units.summary: Use oxidation numbers to explain disproportionation in the reaction of bromine with sodium hydroxide.

units.label: 4(a)
units.summary: Predict the O=N-Cl bond angle in NOCl and explain it.
units.difficulty_basis: Shape with a lone pair on an unfamiliar molecule

units.label: 4(b)(i)
units.summary: Write the Kc expression for the dissociation of NOCl.

units.label: 4(b)(ii)
units.summary: Explain how the concentration of NO was found from that of chlorine.

units.label: 4(b)(iii)
units.summary: Calculate the equilibrium concentration of NOCl from Kc and concentrations of NO and Cl2.
units.difficulty_basis: Rearranged Kc with a square root

units.label: 4(b)(iv)
units.summary: State and explain the effect of raising temperature on the equilibrium concentration of NO.

units.label: 5(a)
units.summary: Identify which of six skeletal alcohols are secondary.

units.label: 5(b)
units.summary: Complete the equation for complete combustion of butan-2-ol.

units.label: 5(c)
units.summary: Give the systematic name of a skeletal alcohol.

units.label: 5(d)(i)
units.summary: Calculate the atom economy for preparing the alcohol by hydrolysis of the bromoalkane.
units.difficulty_basis: Mr calculation for reactants and products

units.label: 5(d)(ii)
units.summary: Outline the mechanism for alkaline hydrolysis of a primary bromoalkane.
units.difficulty_basis: Mechanism with curly arrows dipoles and lone pairs

units.label: 5(d)(iii)
units.summary: Name the type of mechanism shown.

units.label: 5(e)
units.summary: State and explain how the rate of hydrolysis differs for a chloroalkane and a bromoalkane.

units.label: 5(f)
units.summary: Identify the alcohol and its oxidation product from mass and IR spectra and write the oxidation equation.
units.difficulty_basis: Extended synoptic deduction from spectra and reaction
